clue.text: Not all bound over being set free

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A court lets someone off with a bind-over, so they are not entirely free.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen or unfasten something is to release it, so the verb fits a sense of setting free.

clue.text: Peacekeepers beginning to be inappropriate

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
becoming means starting to be, coming into a state

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers starting to behave in an unsuitable way.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbecoming behaviour is unseemly or unsuitable, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Conscientious university ousted revolutionary

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things over completely, so these letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A diligent university has expelled a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousted' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is fodder: U plus OUSTED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Duteous is an old word for dutiful, someone who carefully does what is required.

clue.text: An hour with Ephemeris perhaps covers half the world

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hour

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible rearrangement of the word before it rather than the word itself

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronomical table of positions, the Ephemeris, takes in half the globe within an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: An ephemeris is an almanac of star and planet positions; here its letters are rearranged to EMISPHERE after H.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemisphere is one half of the globe, divided by the equator or a meridian.

clue.text: Liberal piece of cake disappearing

parts.note: a piece of cake is something easy
going means leaving or vanishing

explanation.surface: A generous person's slice of cake vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberal, tolerant attitude is a relaxed, permissive one.

clue.text: Home help moving up-country

parts.note: being at home is being in

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving up means the word help is read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: A domestic helper relocates to the country areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up-country' looks like one word, but 'up' belongs with 'moving' as the reversal signal, leaving 'country' as the definition. IN plus DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: India is an example of a country.

clue.text: Hamlet baffling? Pretend to be indifferent

parts.note: Hamlet is a play by Shakespeare
something baffling is hard to get, difficult to understand

explanation.surface: Someone finds Hamlet puzzling and then shrugs it off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes feigning lack of interest to seem more desirable.

clue.text: Concern raised about a man's otitis

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes around the next letter
in a down clue, raised means the word concern is read upwards

parts.note: care means concern
he stands for a man; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Worry is voiced about a fellow's ear infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' looks like worry, and 'otitis' is a medical term for ear inflammation; the 's of man's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Otitis is inflammation of the ear, which causes pain in the ear.

clue.text: Little girl melted me with goodness

indicators.note: melted means the shape of the word me is changed

parts.note: my! is an exclamation like goodness!

explanation.surface: A little girl softened me with her kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goodness' looks like virtue but is the exclamation 'my!'; ME rearranged gives EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmy is a girl's name, a pet form of Emma or Emily.

clue.text: Page showing mushrooms

explanation.surface: A page of a book displays fungi.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime (a Christmas stage show), Cinderella's loyal page is called Buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttons is the traditional name of the pageboy in pantomime Cinderella, and button mushrooms are small young ones.

clue.text: See a beaver rootle around, and give complicated explanation

indicators.note: around signals that the letters are moved about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Watch a beaver root about, then explain it in too much detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a link here; the anagram fodder is 'a beaver rootle', thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To overelaborate is to explain or develop something in excessive detail.

clue.text: Girl with a weight chart

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A girl holding a weight beside a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a drawing or chart showing information.

clue.text: Nothing more than routine work, illustrative of dance composition

indicators.note: more than means the letter for nothing comes after, added to, the piece for routine work

parts.note: a chore is routine work
O, the figure zero, means nothing
graphic means illustrative, pictorial

explanation.surface: A dance's composition is described as merely routine work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing more than' reads as 'merely', but it is O placed after CHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Choreography is the composing of dance steps, and the adjective relates to it.

clue.text: Where to go 'off for a different course

definitions.text: Where to go 'off for a different course

parts.words: Where to go 'off for a different course
parts.note: going off at an angle from a curve describes the geometric line touching it, and also drifting from the topic

explanation.surface: Directions for leaving the route on a new heading.
explanation.definitionFit: To go off at a tangent is to digress suddenly onto a different subject.

clue.text: Service end of cue for this stroke

parts.note: the Catholic Eucharist is a church service of this name

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word cue

explanation.surface: A church service ends with a billiard shot.
explanation.walkthrough: A massé is a billiards shot played with the cue held nearly upright to make the ball curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A massé is a particular stroke in billiards.

clue.text: Tense, being immature

explanation.surface: Being young and nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperfect is a grammatical tense, and imperfect also means not fully formed or developed.

clue.text: Parking space, needed —— that's nothing new

parts.note: latitude means scope or room to move

explanation.surface: A parking space is needed, says someone stating the obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a stale remark, a commonplace with no fresh thought.

clue.text: Yearning to be free, lost again

indicators.note: free means the letters are loosened and rearranged

explanation.surface: Wishing to be released after losing once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a wistful longing for the past.

clue.text: Sound's turned up to catch point in meeting

indicators.note: to catch means the reversed word holds the next letter inside
in a down clue, turned up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: noise is sound; the 's gives the plural noises
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Sound is raised to hear a point made in a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes SESION from NOISES, and 'to catch' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A session is a meeting or sitting of a body for business.

clue.text: One may be tickled to death

definitions.text: One may be tickled to death

parts.words: One may be tickled to death
parts.note: being delighted is the surface; poachers literally tickle a river fish under its belly to catch it

explanation.surface: Someone who could be thoroughly delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish tickling is a poaching method: stroking a trout's underside until it can be flipped out of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout are the fish classically caught by tickling.

clue.text: Terrifyingly big, but his gore was shed

indicators.note: being shed, cast off and scattered, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something huge and frightening, though its blood was spilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogreish means like an ogre, a huge, frightening giant.

clue.text: Evening at club provides goose

parts.note: evening out a surface is smoothing it
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A night at the club supplies a goose for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' looks like time of day but means making even; a tailor's goose is a heavy smoothing iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose is a tailor's heavy pressing iron with a curved handle.

clue.text: One taking things amiss

parts.note: taking things amiss reads as being offended, but here means taking things wrongly, unlawfully

explanation.surface: A touchy person who takes offence.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief takes other people's property wrongfully.

clue.text: Make officer appear an idiot

parts.note: to do is to make or carry out
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: Making an officer look foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolt is a stupid person, a synonym of idiot.

clue.text: Japanese enterprise folding

parts.note: a Japanese business going under is the surface; read literally it is a Japanese pursuit done by folding paper

explanation.surface: A Japanese company is going out of business.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: Take the string off new unit ——it's in knots

indicators.note: being tied in knots means these letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Unwrapping a new piece of kit whose string is knotted.
explanation.definitionFit: To untwine is to unwind or untwist string or cord.

clue.text: New arrivals from truck charge to back of tent

parts.note: a tender is a wagon attached to a locomotive carrying fuel and water
a fee is a charge

indicators.note: back of picks the last letter of the word tent

explanation.surface: Newcomers pay a charge on a lorry to camp at the back of a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderfeet are newcomers or novices unused to hardship.

clue.text: Good deerstalker in mountain pass

parts.note: a deerstalker is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A fine deerstalker cap worn in a mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a ghat is a mountain pass, as well as steps down to a river.
